messages:
jamie.dev: FYI running into a weird edge-case in the sample app when using the JS SDK in JSON mode + function/tool-calling. The runtime sometimes returns an array for the tool output but the SDK helper strictly expects an object and throws during parse.

samir: ugh. do we have a repro? is it the sample recipe or the helper shim?

jamie.dev: Repro steps below. Happens intermittently when a function returns multiple suggestions (we return them as an array on purpose). The JS helper's validator runs a strict schema expecting properties like `choice` and `meta` on the root object. When it sees `[]` it errors out and the whole request is retried by our auth/retry middleware which replays the function call and ends up duplicating telemetry and confusing the caller.

lia: can you paste the exact prompt + schema and the failing response?

jamie.dev: sure — here's the relevant bits from the sample app: 

```js
const schema = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    choice: { type: 'string' },
    meta: { type: 'object' }
  },
  required: ['choice']
}

// we call a tool that suggests multiple variants intentionally
// tool returns: [ { choice: 'A' }, { choice: 'B' } ]

const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'redwood/sample-tool',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }],
  json_schema: schema,
  json_mode: true,
  functions: [ /* ... */ ]
})
```

jamie.dev: And the actual failing response we saw from the model/runtime (logged):

```
tool_output: [ { "choice": "A" }, { "choice": "B" } ]
error: schema validation failed: expected object, got array
```

samir: So the runtime returns an array, which is valid for some tool contracts, but the sample app's schema didn't account for array-of-choices. Two problems: (1) SDK helper should surface a nicer error and not crash the whole flow, (2) auth/retry middleware shouldn't blindly replay the function call when the error is a client-side validation mismatch.

lia: Also parity note: our Py SDK maps this to a list and returns it cleanly — the JS SDK currently coalesces into the helper and runs `validateStrict(schema, parsed)` which throws. We need consistent behavior across SDKs.

jamie.dev: Proposal: change the JS helper to attempt to coerce array => object when schema expects an object by wrapping: `{ choice: arr[0]?.choice, meta: arr[0]?.meta }` as a fallback, but only when `json_mode` true and the app opts in to permissive parsing. Otherwise surface a 4xx-ish ValidationError with clear payload. Also stop the retry on ValidationError.

samir: I prefer not to auto-coerce silently. Make it opt-in. Add a `permissive_json_parsing: true` option at request-level or SDK-client-level. If true, helper may attempt mild coercions and add a `sdk_parsed_hint` field into the returned object.

lia: Agree on opt-in. For retries: middleware should treat schema ValidationError as terminal (no retry) — but distinguish between transient runtime errors (5xx) vs client parse errors. We already have an error codemap in the auth middleware but it seems ValidationError was falling into the retryable bucket because it's thrown after we parse the network response.

jamie.dev: I'll open a PR with two commits: (1) make ValidationError a distinct Error subclass with code `INVALID_SCHEMA` and the middleware will not retry `INVALID_SCHEMA`; (2) add `permissiveJsonParsing` flag to the JS helper and a minimal coercion implementation plus an opt-in telemetry hint.

samir: Sounds good. Can you include a unit test that simulates tool output as array and asserts both modes (strict => throw, permissive => return coerced object + sdk_parsed_hint)?

jamie.dev: Yup — adding tests and an e2e playground sample update. Also adding an entry in sample-app README describing when to use array-of-results vs single-object tool-call patterns.

lia: For parity, can you add an analogous flag to the Python SDK (maybe `permissive_json_parsing=False` default) and document behavior. Keep defaults strict.

jamie.dev: Will do. One more gotcha: CI flaky test triggered by deploy-bot because our auth retry logic increments a request-retry counter metric — the double-replay due to parse error causes the deploy-bot to alert on duplicate idempotency keys. Fixing the middleware retry policy should stop the noise.

ci-bot: [deploy bot] alert suppressed: increased duplicate-idempotency alerts during 2026-03-10 09:12:xx due to client-side validation issues (investigating).

samir: Thanks — can you link the PR here once open and tag @eng-runtime and @devex? I'll review the middleware changes.

jamie.dev: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/842 — includes changelog, tests, and sample-app README update. Tagging @eng-runtime @devex.

lia: Quick checklist for the PR: 
- mark ValidationError as non-retryable in auth middleware
- add permissiveJsonParsing opt-in and unit tests
- update sample-app README with recommended tool output shapes
- add integration test that simulates duplicate telemetry prevention

samir: also add a runtime note in docs: "If your tool can return multiple alternatives, prefer returning an object wrapper: { variants: [...] } so schema can describe it explicitly."

jamie.dev: Will add. Thanks all :rocket:

samir: :thumbsup:
